slot.brief: Body starting from rest with uniform acceleration; find distance covered in a specific (nth) second using the nth-second formula.

stem: A cart starts from rest and moves along a straight track with constant acceleration of $4\ \text{m s}^{-2}$. How far does it travel during the fifth second?

verdicts.working: Distance in the fifth second = ½(4)(5² − 4²) = 18 m.

working:
$s_n=u+\dfrac{a}{2}(2n-1)$
$u=0,\ a=4\ \text{m s}^{-2},\ n=5$
$s_5=\dfrac{4}{2}(9)=18\ \text{m}$

Independent check: Distance in the fifth second = ½(4)(5² − 4²) = 18 m.
solution:
Distance travelled in the $n$th second is $s_n=u+\dfrac{a}{2}(2n-1)$.
$$s_5=0+\dfrac{4}{2}(2\cdot5-1)=18\ \text{m}$$
